thread:
Ajay: Heads-up — been pairing with SRE on the enqueue/batching abstraction for observability ingest. Found tradeoffs we should call out before the RFC follow-up.
Taylor: +1, curious which tradeoffs. short summary?
Ajay: tl;dr: three options — 1) edge enqueue + shard-aware batching in central worker, 2) centralized enqueue & batch scheduler, 3) hybrid where edge only tags and central does everything. Costs/latency/operational surface differ.
Maria: can you sketch the main failure modes we care about? e.g., backpressure ripple, duplicate attribution, or lost billing keys?
Ajay: exactly. failure modes: A) hotspot/backpressure at enqueue node -> request drop or head-of-line latency, B) lost/stripped attributes when edge minifies headers, C) batch re-ordering that breaks time-windowed cost attribution.
Devin: also add: observability query shape depends on envelope granularity. If edges compact too aggressively we lose join keys for cost stitching.
Taylor: what about caching prefixes at edge? reduces central load, but makes invalidation + freshness tricky for billing keys.
Ajay: we prototyped prefix-caching: wins ~30% peak tokens to central, but introduced ~5s attribution skew under churn. Not huge, but visible in SLA tests.
Maria: hmm. For regulated customers we probably can't accept that skew. Maybe make caching opt-in per tenant?
Devin: +1 opt-in. Also consider hybrid safety pattern: edge caches, but attaches a stable canonical header that central honors if present. If not, central falls back to full enrich, no cache response.
Taylor: how does that look in config? e.g.:
```
edge.conf:
  caching: enabled
  canonical_key_header: X-RW-CANONICAL
central.conf:
  honor_canonical: true
  fallback_enrich: true
```
Ajay: yeah. Need a migration plan: enable for tenant in "observe" mode (honor but don't trust) -> compare canonical vs enriched outcome -> promote.
ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: ingest-edge v2 -> 2026-04-02 03:00 UTC, will route 10% traffic to canaries :rocket:
Maria: Another interface boundary: who owns time-windowing semantics? If batching reorders events across minute boundaries, cost aggregation breaks. Declare "batcher must preserve event_time monotonicity per tenant" as an invariant.
Devin: Implementation: add sequence-number per tenant+stream and include first_event_ts,last_event_ts in batch envelope. Central stitcher uses them to place tokens into correct buckets.
Taylor: sequence numbers increase envelope size. Any numbers on overhead?
Ajay: measurement: +12 bytes per event for 64-bit seq + 8 byte ts ~ negligible vs payload, but gives determinism.
Maria: cross-region fallback concern: routing to another region can change cost attribution if keys normalized differently.
Devin: propose canonicalization library shipped as a tiny deterministic module in all regions so normalization identical. Include "region_id" in metadata to debug mismatches.
Taylor: permissions: who flips opt-ins? product? platform? need RBAC for tenant-level cache opt-in.
Ajay: Platform toggles, product triggers via onboarding. Add audit log entry for any opt-in toggle.
Maria: observability of the observability pipeline: token-level cost meters, queue depth histograms per shard, per-tenant attribution mismatch alert.
Taylor: add a lightweight probe sampling 1/10k events that records full enrich vs canonical output diff, to feed regression alerts.
Devin: helps Optimize automation too — flag when canonicalization drift > X%.
Ajay: next steps: I'll update the follow-up RFC with: invariants (monotonicity, canonical header semantics), opt-in flow, sequence numbers, audit events, sampling probe. Ping me if you want a short appendix with the experimental numbers.
Maria: tagging @Taylor for ops RBAC, @Devin for canonical lib, and @Ajay to draft the RFC appendix. :thumbsup:
Taylor: noted, will add RBAC snippet and a minimal policy schema.
Ajay: thanks — I'll post the draft tomorrow morning and open the RFC thread. End of thread.
